Understanding one teaches nothing about the other; the only link is diff adjacency, which B cites merely to justify treating the pre-existing validator path as touched.

Both findings describe the same attack chain (branch-controlled failureSummary reaching a contents:write, Bash-enabled agent), but each names a different broken link. A's mechanism is authorization: `allowed_bots` disables claude-code-action's non-bot actor guard on both agent jobs, removing the last automatic human-in-the-loop signal so the bot's own push closes the loop unattended; the fix concerns who may trigger the job. B's mechanism is prompt construction: line 165 splices `steps.diag.outputs.summary` in with no "this is DATA" wrapper or delimiter, and the review-panel's `<panel-findings>` fence is escapable because the enclosed lens text is unescaped; the fix concerns how untrusted text is framed. Restoring the actor guard leaves the unfenced interpolation and the closeable `</panel-findings>` tag fully exploitable on human-triggered runs. Adding a non-closeable fence leaves A's complaint intact: the secret-bearing jobs still run with no human gate. B itself treats `allowed_bots` as background ("Both channels only became live with this diff's allowed_bots"), not as its defect.

Same feature (the new POST /internal/yorkie/events → touchUpdatedAt path) but two distinct causes with opposite failure modes. A: migration scripts' doc.update() rewrites emit DocumentRootChanged for every document, and nothing marks them as non-user edits, so updatedAt is mass-bumped to the migration timestamp and list ordering collapses fleet-wide; fix is in the scripts or an admin-client exclusion. B: the handler's `Math.min(issuedMs, now)` has no lower bound, so a Go zero time / bogus past value produces an `at` in the far past, `where updatedAt < at` matches nothing, and a genuine edit is silently dropped; fix is a `ms <= 0 → now` fallback. Adding the lower-bound fallback would not stop bulk scripts from bumping updatedAt — it falls back to `now`, precisely the value A objects to. Excluding migration/admin clients would leave the epoch-zero silent drop fully intact for normal user edits. Each finding stands after the other is fixed; the shared touchUpdatedAt call is a common surface, not a common root cause.

A is a security/authorization defect: the store's write-capable undo()/redo() (yorkie-note-store.ts:93) mutate the shared CRDT with no readOnly gate, relying solely on view-level gates (keymap replaced by [], EditorView.editable, toolbar canFormat) plus a webhook that defaults to permissive shadow mode. B is a coverage gap: routeVimHistoryToStore's monkey-patch of CodeMirror.commands.undo/redo (editor.ts:29-60) has no test — editor.test.ts never presses u/<C-r> nor inspects store history, so a regression makes vim undo a silent no-op. Adding a readOnly check inside the store would not create any test for the vim routing branches; writing those tests would not place an authorization check on the writing operation. B's 'view is editable' branch appears in A only as one of the fragile gates cited as evidence, not as A's subject. Per the rubric, a defect and missing test coverage are not one defect.
